page: Amazon Web Services i2.8xlarge is a legacy generation, storage-optimized virtual machine provisioned on the Xen hypervisor. It is powered by the Intel Xeon E5-2670 v2 processor operating at 2.5 GHz, providing 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The instance is configured with 244.0 GB of system memory, averaging 7.62 GB per vCPU, and includes 6,400 GB of directly attached local SSD storage. Network connectivity is rated at a 10 Gbps baseline bandwidth, and no GPU hardware is present.

Benchmark results demonstrate the architectural characteristics of the underlying Ivy Bridge hardware. Single-core throughput is constrained, reflected by a Geekbench single-core score of 534.0 and single-threaded bzip3 decompression at 7.4 GB/sec, placing in the lower percentiles. In contrast, multi-threaded metrics remain competitive for general data processing, achieving a PassMark CPU score of 29,387.12, multi-core stress-ng at 27,789.21, and Redis SET throughput exceeding 11.15 million operations per second. Memory bandwidth yields 82.93 GB/sec on uncached 256 MB read blocks and 37.47 GB/sec on writes.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the resource profile prioritizes dense local solid-state storage and memory capacity over single-thread compute efficiency. The inclusion of 6,400 GB bundled local SSD eliminates external EBS transfer latency and attached volume fees for high-IOPS applications. The trade-off is the older CPU microarchitecture lacking newer vector instruction sets like AVX-512, which diminishes suitability for modern instruction-heavy operations and large language model inference.

The i2.8xlarge instance fits I/O-intensive workloads requiring large amounts of local scratch space or fast disk access. It is appropriate for relational databases, distributed NoSQL datastores, Redis caching layers, and high-throughput data warehousing tasks.

The configuration allocates 32 dedicated vCPUs from 16 physical cores, 244.0 GB of RAM, and 6,400 GB of bundled local SSD storage, backed by a 10 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance shows average multi-core processing with a PassMark CPU score of 29,387.12 and 11.15 million Redis SET operations per second, though single-core metrics like the Geekbench single-core score of 534.0 reflect older CPU silicon. The substantial integrated local SSD capacity provides high throughput for I/O-heavy applications without additional attached storage costs. This configuration is suited for large transactional databases, distributed NoSQL systems, in-memory caches, and batch ETL data processing.
